proposals.title: Say the app serves eight MCP tools, not seven
proposals.rationale: The module map says seven forge-mcp-2 tools; the dispatch door lists eight.
proposals.body:
## Summary
The Forge app doc undercounts its MCP tools.

## Description
The module map in `docs/forge-app.md` names seven tools, while `TOOL_NAMES` holds eight since `dowser_direction_get` landed.

## Flow
- read the module map
- connect a coding agent
- see a tool the doc does not name

## Expected impact
A judge reading the doc sees the tool list the agent sees.

## Evaluation
The module map names every entry of `TOOL_NAMES`.

evidence.quote: | `rovo:mcp` | `dowser-mcp` | `mcp` | The seven forge-mcp-2 tools, for Claude Code and Codex CLI |
/** The eight forge-mcp-2 tools (reflect_sync and direction_get are additive to the original six). */

proposals.confidence_why: the doc line and the code line contradict each other directly

proposals.title: Accept several proposals at once
proposals.rationale: Reject and snooze take many refs; accept takes one, so a good scan is accepted card by card.
proposals.body:
## Summary
Let a person accept a selection of proposals in one step.

## Description
`accept` creates one Jira issue per call while `reject` and `snooze` already take a list of refs.

## Flow
- select the cards to keep
- accept them together
- get one issue per card

## Expected impact
Fewer clicks after a strong scan.

## Evaluation
Time from first to last decision on a push drops.

proposals.title: Decide whether plain http repo links stay allowed
proposals.rationale: A pushed repo_url may be http, so evidence links can point at an unencrypted host.
proposals.body:
## Summary
Repo links accept `http:` as well as `https:`.

## Description
`webRepoUrl` keeps an http remote so self-hosted servers link at all; the inbox then shows plain http links.

## Flow
- push from an http remote
- open an evidence link
- the browser loads it unencrypted

## Expected impact
A documented, deliberate choice either way.

## Evaluation
The security notes say which schemes a repo link may use.

proposals.title: Show progress when an accept is already running
proposals.rationale: A second click on Accept answers 'reload in a minute' with nothing to watch.
proposals.body:
## Summary
A repeated accept tells the person to wait without showing what is happening.

## Description
The accept claim refuses a second accept for two minutes and answers with a reload hint.

## Flow
- click Accept
- click it again while Jira is slow
- read reload in a minute

## Expected impact
No duplicate clicks and no guessing.

## Evaluation
Fewer repeated accepts per issue created.

evidence.quote: throw new AppError('bad-input', `an accept of ${p.ref} is already in progress; reload in a minute`);

proposals.confidence_why: the message is in the code; how often it shows is not measured
